audit.whatIsWrong: Tangle-Barbs is the tracked ability in every string of both layers and its upgrade condition is never stated. breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].d get as far as 'extends through targets. Dodge it.'
audit.why: Riot: 'Neeko slings a tangle that damages and roots everything it passes through. If the tangle KILLS an enemy or PASSES THROUGH A CHAMPION, it becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer.' That means the minion wave is not cover — it is an amplifier. A tangle that executes a low minion on its way arrives bigger, quicker and with a longer root, so the safest place to stand is not behind the wave but away from the line entirely. It is 1000 range on 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, against Chomp's 300.
audit.corrected: Tangle-Barbs is a 1000-range line on 12s at rank 1 that roots everything it passes through, and it grows larger, faster and longer-rooting if it kills a unit or passes a champion first — so a low minion in its path upgrades the root that reaches you.

audit.whatIsWrong: mid and spikes[1] both say Pillar of Ice answers Pop Blossom — 'Pillar only cancels the channel if it displaces her', 'Pillar toward her immediately — that forces her to cancel the channel or eat the terrain', and wants.foe[1] says she wants an angle 'where Pillar cannot interrupt the wind-up'.
audit.why: Pillar of Ice creates impassable terrain and slows; it displaces nobody, so the entry's own conditional never fires. And Riot gives a much better tell for free: 'The preparation is hidden if Neeko is disguised.' That means the wind-up is visible whenever she is not wearing someone else's face, and invisible precisely when she is — so the read is her disguise state, not a race between two cooldowns. Pop Blossom also has a 600 radius, so stepping out is a distance problem with a number on it.
audit.corrected: Pop Blossom's preparation is hidden only while she is disguised — that is the tell. It reaches 600, so leave the radius rather than trying to answer it with a pillar that displaces nothing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (R Pop Blossom, cd 120/105/90, range 600; P Inherent Glamour)
champ-data/_kits/trundle.json (E Pillar of Ice, terrain + slow)

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown or range appears anywhere in either layer, and Shapesplitter is mentioned only as a way for her to be somewhere unexpected.
audit.why: Shapesplitter's passive is the half that matters in a lane against Trundle: bonus magic damage on every third attack plus a brief move-speed boost. That is both her sustained damage in the trade Frozen Domain wants to force, and the tool that lets her leave the ice — which the entry attributes vaguely to 'her kite' three times. The clone is 16s at rank 1. Blooming Burst is 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 at 800. And Pop Blossom is 120/105/90 against Subjugate's 120/100/80, so Trundle's ultimate is level at rank 1 and back first from rank 2 onward.
audit.corrected: Blooming Burst 9s at 800. Shapesplitter 16s, with a passive giving bonus magic damage and move speed every third attack. Pop Blossom 120/105/90 against Subjugate 120/100/80.
sources: champ-data/_kits/neeko.json (Q cd 9/8.5/8/7.5/7 range 800; W Shapesplitter cd 16/15/14/13/12; R cd 120/105/90)

audit.whatIsWrong: Three stages are labelled against their own reasoning. win[2] reads Skill while whys[2] opens 'Neeko edges level 3'. win[4] reads Skill while whys[4] ends 'she edges this window'. win[6] reads Neeko while whys[6] ends 'extended duels are yours and she cannot win the side lane'.
audit.why: The packet has 50.44% over 113 games, so a mostly-Skill chart is defensible in aggregate — but not at the three stages where the prose states a winner outright and the chart says something else. The two-item stage is the clearest error: the entry argues at length that Subjugate plus Frozen Domain wins the side-lane duel and then labels the stage Neeko.
audit.corrected: Level 3 Neeko, Level 6 Neeko, two-plus items Trundle — matching the three whys that name a winner.

edits.before: Level 1 is a fair stand-off: Chomp on her first last-hit attempt wins the exchange — the bite damage plus the immediate AD steal and your passive healing off minion deaths makes even the opening trade yours on paper — but she has Blooming Burst (Q) to chip you back and range to disengage before you get a second Chomp off, so it stays even in practice. Level 2 you get Frozen Domain and the lane becomes about positioning: if she ever stands inside your W zone while trading, she is losing slowly and she knows it, so she will kite the ice patch. Respect that kite rather than burning Pillar trying to catch her before you have the full kit. At Level 3 she gets the advantage — her Tangle-Barbs (E) root gives her a punish window that your two-ability kit cannot fully answer yet: she roots you, re-blooms Q on top, and then backs out before Chomp even cools down. Never charge forward into Tangle-Barbs range with your W already placed — place it only after she wastes the root.
edits.after: Level 1 is a fair stand-off: Chomp on her first last-hit attempt wins the exchange — a flat 3.5s bite that saps her AD, plus King's Tribute healing off dying minions — but Blooming Burst reaches 800 and re-blooms on champion contact, so she chips back before your second bite and it stays even in practice. Level 2 you get Frozen Domain and the lane becomes positioning: if she ever trades inside your ice she is losing slowly and she knows it, so she will kite the patch. Respect that kite rather than burning Pillar before you have the full kit. At Level 3 she takes the advantage — Tangle-Barbs is a 1000-range line on 12s that roots everything it passes through, and it grows larger, faster and longer-rooting if it kills a unit or passes a champion first. So the wave is no shield: a low minion in its path upgrades the root that reaches you. Never walk into that range with W already placed — place it after she spends the root.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you split trades: farm with Chomp and keep Frozen Domain ready, but do not chase her outside the ice patch because your move speed advantage disappears the instant you step off it. The core discipline is treating Tangle-Barbs like a red light — when it is down, run the full pattern; when it is up, give nothing and let her waste it on a minion. Level 6 is her next spike: Pop Blossom set up from a clone or W-invisible angle is genuinely dangerous because Pillar only cancels the channel if it displaces her, and if she pre-positioned with Shapesplitter (W) you may not know where she actually is. When you see a Neeko standing suspiciously still, Pillar toward her immediately — that forces her to cancel the channel or eat the terrain. Do not Subjugate early thinking the stat drain gives you the all-in if Pop Blossom is still up; drain first and fight second only if you confirmed her ult is spent or interrupted.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you split trades: farm with Chomp and keep Frozen Domain ready, but do not chase her off the ice, because your move-speed edge ends the instant you step off it — and Shapesplitter's passive hands her bonus magic damage plus move speed on every third attack, so the running fight is hers. The discipline is treating Tangle-Barbs like a red light on its 12s: when it is down run the full pattern, when it is up give nothing and let her spend it on a minion. Level 6 is her next spike, but the timers favour you — Pop Blossom is 120/105/90 against your 120/100/80, level at rank 1 and yours first from rank 2. Its preparation is hidden only while she is disguised, so a Neeko wearing an ally's face is the read, and the answer is leaving the 600 radius rather than racing the cast. Do not open with Subjugate while Pop Blossom is still held.

edits.before: Two items is your home territory. Subjugate drains Neeko's thin magic resistance directly onto you — she is a squishy AP mage with no innate tankiness to feed the steal, but even a moderate MR transfer combined with Frozen Domain's healing means your sustain in an extended fight far exceeds what a single Q-E-R AP rotation can erase. She needs to kill you in one burst cycle; you need to stay alive until Chomp stacks the AD theft and your W healing compounds. If she blows Pop Blossom and misses or you Pillar her out of the channel, the window is over and you win the extended duel cleanly. Respect her as a split-push nuisance who can disguise and roam, but in a straight side-lane 1v1 with your item spike active she has to land every ability to survive and you only need Frozen Domain and patience.
edits.after: Two items is your home territory. Subjugate takes a percentage of Neeko's Health, Armor and MR and doubles the theft over four seconds — she is squishy, so the numbers are modest, but with Frozen Domain amplifying your healing your sustain in an extended fight far exceeds what a single Q-E-R rotation erases. She needs to kill you in one burst cycle; you need to live until Chomp's 3.5s has stacked the AD theft and the W healing compounds. If Pop Blossom misses, the window is gone and the duel is cleanly yours — and at 120/105/90 against your 120/100/80 you reach the next one first. Respect her as a roaming nuisance who can wear an ally's face, but in a side-lane 1v1 she has to land everything and you need only Frozen Domain and patience.

notes: BIGGEST ADD: Tangle-Barbs 'becomes larger, faster, and roots for longer' if it kills an enemy or passes through a champion. Every string in both layers tracked this ability and none of them said so, and the practical consequence inverts the usual instinct — standing behind a low minion makes the root that reaches you bigger, not smaller. CORRECTED: mid, spikes[1] and wants.foe[1] all build a plan around Pillar of Ice interrupting Pop Blossom, including the self-defeating clause 'Pillar only cancels the channel if it displaces her'. Pillar creates terrain and slows; it displaces nothing. Riot supplies a far better tell for free — the preparation is hidden ONLY while she is disguised — so the read is her disguise state, and the answer is leaving the 600 radius. ADDED: Shapesplitter's passive (bonus magic damage and move speed every third attack) was absent from both layers, and it is what her kiting and her sustained damage actually run on; the entry attributed both to 'her kite' three times with nothing behind it. NUMBERS: Blooming Burst 9s at 800, Tangle-Barbs 12s at 1000, Shapesplitter 16s, Pop Blossom 120/105/90 against Subjugate's 120/100/80 — level at rank 1 and Trundle's first from rank 2 onward. Not one cooldown appeared anywhere in the entry before this. FIXED: tldr and winCon call Neeko 'him'. UNVERIFIED, LEFT ALONE: the entry twice describes a 'W-invisible angle'. Riot's text for Shapesplitter describes a passive third-attack bonus and a directional clone, with no invisibility, and the kit file carries no stealth flag on it, so I rewrote those clauses around the clone and the disguise rather than asserting or denying invisibility. NOT EDITED (enum): three stages contradict their own whys — win[2] reads Skill under a why that opens 'Neeko edges level 3', win[4] reads Skill under a why ending 'she edges this window', and win[6] reads Neeko under a why ending 'extended duels are yours and she cannot win the side lane'.
